title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 44
paragraphs: After the inquiry about the oracles and the exhortation given by Mardonius, night came on and the guards were set. When night was well advanced and it seemed that there was quiet everywhere in the camps, the men being in their deepest sleep, then Alexander son of Amyntas, commander and king of the Macedonians, rode his horse up to the Athenian guard-posts and asked to have speech with their generals. While the greater number of the guards stayed at their posts, some ran to the generals, and when they reached them they said that a man had come riding on a horse out of the Median camp who revealed nothing further, only named the generals and said he wished to have speech with them.
